questions.question: If 2 sin 3θ = 1, then the value of θ is∶
What is the value of frac{3 operatorname{cosec} 42circ}{sec 48circ}-frac{5 cos 32circ}{sin 58circ}
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify **complementary angles**: 42° + 48° = 90° and 32° + 58° = 90°.

Using the property: If **A + B = 90°**, then **csc A / sec B = 1** and **cos A / sin B = 1**.

Expression = 3(1) − 5(1)

Expression = 3 − 5 = −2.

**∴ The correct answer is -2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (3 csc 42° / sec 48°) − (5 cos 32° / sin 58°)

**Formula Used:** csc θ = sec(90° − θ) and cos θ = sin(90° − θ)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/35fba40671bdd4aef535d575a0fde5404dfd08811b008df290d5d93d76829d3f.png] 

⇒ csc 42° = sec(90° − 42°) = sec 48°

⇒ cos 32° = sin(90° − 32°) = sin 58°

⇒ Expression = [3 × sec 48° / sec 48°] − [5 × sin 58° / sin 58°]

⇒ Expression = 3(1) − 5(1)

⇒ Expression = 3 − 5 = −2

**∴ The correct answer is -2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios of Complementary Angles

Two angles are complementary if their sum is 90°. Basic identities include sin(90° − θ) = cos θ and tan(90° − θ) = cot θ.

Secant and Cosecant Relationship

The secant of an angle is equal to the cosecant of its complement: sec θ = csc(90° − θ).

Quotient Property for Complementary Angles

If A + B = 90°, then sin A / cos B = 1, tan A / cot B = 1, and sec A / csc B = 1.</p

If 8cotθ = 7, then the value of (1+sin theta)/(costheta) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given 8cotθ = 7 ⇒ cotθ = 7/8 ⇒ Base (B) = 7, Perpendicular (P) = 8.

Hypotenuse (H) = √(B² + P²) = √(7² + 8²) = √113.

We need to find: (1 + sinθ) / cosθ

Convert to P, B, H: (1 + P/H) / (B/H) = (H + P) / B.

Substitute the direct values: (√113 + 8) / 7 = (8 + √113) / 7.

**∴ The correct answer is (8 + √113)/7.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

8cotθ = 7 ⇒ cotθ = 7/8

**Formula Used:**

cotθ = Base / Perpendicular

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/80f6b7ab00ac5691e58dfe284e020f241f104f5ade8cfb12b08b20fe0df1970e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Base (B) = 7 and Perpendicular (P) = 8

⇒ Hypotenuse (H) = √(8² + 7²)

⇒ H = √(64 + 49) = √113

⇒ sinθ = P / H = 8 / √113

⇒ cosθ = B / H = 7 / √113

⇒ Expression = (1 + sinθ) / cosθ

⇒ = (1 + 8/√113) / (7/√113)

⇒ = [(√113 + 8) / √113] × [√113 / 7]

⇒ = (8 + √113) / 7

**∴ The correct answer is (8 + √113)/7.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

sinθ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse, cosθ = Base / Hypotenuse, tanθ = Perpendicular / Base.

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the base and the perpendicular: H² = P² + B².

Basic Trigonometric Identities

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 | sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 | cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.
</p

questions.question: In a right angle ΔABC, ∠B = 90°, if tanA = 1, then 4 sinA cosA = ______________.

tanA = 1

sinA = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse

⇒ 4 sinA cosA = 4 × (1 ÷ √2) × (1 ÷ √2)

⇒ Base (B) = √(H² − P²)

⇒ Base (B) = √(5² − 4²) = √(25 − 16) = √9 = 3

Now, finding the required trigonometric ratios:

⇒ sin x = P / H = 4/5

⇒ cos x = B / H = 3/5

⇒ tan x = P / B = 4/3

⇒ cot x = B / P = 3/4

⇒ Numerator = 5 × (4/5)² + 8 × (3/4)²

⇒ Numerator = 5 × (16/25) + 8 × (9/16)

⇒ Numerator = 16/5 + 9/2 = (32 + 45) / 10 = 77/10

Solving the denominator of the expression: 27tan²x − 125cos²x

⇒ Denominator = 27 × (4/3)² − 125 × (3/5)²

⇒ Denominator = 27 × (16/9) − 125 × (9/25)

⇒ Denominator = (3 × 16) − (5 × 9) = 48 − 45 = 3

Dividing numerator by denominator:

⇒ Value = (77/10) ÷ 3 = 77/30

**∴ The correct answer is 77/30.**

questions.question: If θ is an acute angle and tan θ + cot θ = 2, then find the value of tan³ θ + cot³ θ + 6tan³ θ cot² θ.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If **tan θ + cot θ = 2**, this condition is only satisfied when **tan θ = 1** and **cot θ = 1** (since θ = 45°).

Substitute **tan θ = 1** and **cot θ = 1** in the required expression:

Expression = 1³ + 1³ + 6 × 1³ × 1²

Expression = 1 + 1 + 6 = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f8fc21ce1f77e8eb80d753ad4c647fd8528087ee31707968acf70d02c4e058ec.png] 

**Given:** tan θ + cot θ = 2

**Formula Used:** cot θ = 1/tan θ and (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b)

⇒ tan θ + 1/tan θ = 2

⇒ tan² θ + 1 = 2 tan θ

⇒ tan² θ − 2 tan θ + 1 = 0

⇒ (tan θ − 1)² = 0

⇒ tan θ = 1

⇒ cot θ = 1/1 = 1

Now, calculate: tan³ θ + cot³ θ + 6tan³ θ cot² θ

⇒ (1)³ + (1)³ + 6(1)³(1)²

⇒ 1 + 1 + 6 = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

tan θ × cot θ = 1. Similarly, sin θ × cosec θ = 1 and cos θ × sec θ = 1.

Special Case for x + 1/x

If x + 1/x = 2, then xⁿ + 1/xⁿ is always 2 for any positive integer n.

Standard Trig Values

For θ = 45°, tan 45° = 1 and cot 45° = 1. This is the only acute angle satisfying tan θ + cot θ = 2.</p

The expression **(8 sin A − 4 cos A) / (cos A + 2 sin A)** can be converted to **tan A** by dividing both numerator and denominator by **cos A**.

Converted expression = **(8 tan A − 4) / (1 + 2 tan A)**.

Substitute **tan A = 5/6**: (8 × 5/6 − 4) / (1 + 2 × 5/6) = (20/3 − 4) / (1 + 5/3) = (8/3) / (8/3) = **1**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/82549948d21395335a6e22fb935184b6aabe811032c2b3441aa7418fb3d81a55.png] 

**Given:** 6 tan A = 5 in **First Quadrant** (all ratios positive).

⇒ tan A = 5/6 = Perpendicular / Base.

⇒ sin A = 5 / √(5² + 6²) = 5 / √61

⇒ cos A = 6 / √(5² + 6²) = 6 / √61

**Calculation:**

⇒ Value = [8(5/√61) − 4(6/√61)] / [6/√61 + 2(5/√61)]

⇒ Value = [(40 − 24) / √61] / [(6 + 10) / √61]

⇒ Value = 16 / 16

⇒ Value = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

tan A = sin A / cos A. This identity is extremely useful for simplifying expressions involving both **sine** and **cosine** into a single variable.

Quadrant Rules (ASTC)

In the **First Quadrant** (0° to 90°), all trigonometric ratios (sin, cos, tan, etc.) are positive.

Pythagorean Triplets

For any right-angled triangle, h² = p² + b². Common triplets include (3,4,5), (5,12,13), and (8,15,17).</p

questions.question: If (tan(x))/(sec(x)) = (1)/(2) then the value of (sin x + cos x)² is ___.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Simplify the expression: tan(x) ÷ sec(x) = [sin(x) / cos(x)] × cos(x) = sin(x).

Given sin(x) = 1/2, we directly find the angle x = 30°.

Substitute x = 30° into the given equation (sin x + cos x)².

⇒ (sin 30° + cos 30°)² = (1/2 + √3 / 2)² = (1 + √3)² / 4.

⇒ (1 + 3 + 2√3) / 4 = (4 + 2√3) / 4 = (2 + √3) / 2.

**∴ The correct answer is (2 + √3) / 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

tan(x) / sec(x) = 1/2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1dade30b6107d2fd950273d7c00879070da62a60c57a2e555a95dd71d4bb9c87.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ [sin(x) / cos(x)] ÷ [1 / cos(x)] = 1/2

⇒ sin(x) = 1/2

From the right-angled triangle, sin(x) = Opposite / Hypotenuse = 1 / 2.

⇒ By Pythagoras Theorem, Adjacent = √(2² − 1²) = √(4 − 1) = √3

⇒ cos(x) = Adjacent / Hypotenuse = √3 / 2

Now evaluate the given expression: (sin x + cos x)²

⇒ (1/2 + √3 / 2)²

⇒ [(1 + √3) / 2]²

⇒ (1² + (√3)² + 2 × 1 × √3) / 4

⇒ (1 + 3 + 2√3) / 4

⇒ (4 + 2√3) / 4

⇒ 2(2 + √3) / 4 = (2 + √3) / 2

**∴ The correct answer is (2 + √3) / 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

The three core Pythagorean identities are: sin²(x) + cos²(x) = 1, sec²(x) − tan²(x) = 1, and cosec²(x) − cot²(x) = 1.

Standard Angles

Key basic angle values: sin(30°) = 1/2, cos(30°) = √3 / 2, and tan(30°) = 1 / √3. For 60°, the sine and cosine values are swapped.

Reciprocal Ratios

The fundamental reciprocal ratios are: sec(x) = 1 / cos(x), cosec(x) = 1 / sin(x), and cot(x) = 1 / tan(x).
</p

questions.question: If tan (t) = 1/3, what is the value of sec (t)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Using the fundamental trigonometric identity: sec²(t) = 1 + tan²(t)

⇒ sec²(t) = 1 + (1 / 3)² = 1 + 1 / 9 = 10 / 9

⇒ sec(t) = √(10 / 9) = √10 / 3

**∴ The correct answer is √10 / 3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

tan(t) = 1 / 3

**Formula Used:**

tan(t) = Perpendicular / Base

sec(t) = Hypotenuse / Base

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6928b471ceb54a39c3ca280f939d897cbb4ce6b7a14e5e81f3e384e4fd0bcc24.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ By comparing the ratio, let Perpendicular = 1 and Base = 3

⇒ Hypotenuse = √(1² + 3²)

⇒ Hypotenuse = √(1 + 9) = √10

⇒ sec(t) = Hypotenuse / Base

⇒ sec(t) = √10 / 3

**∴ The correct answer is √10 / 3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

The three primary Pythagorean identities are: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of its base and perpendicular: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular².

Trigonometric Ratios

For an angle t in a right triangle: tan(t) = Perpendicular ÷ Base, cos(t) = Base ÷ Hypotenuse, and sec(t) is the reciprocal of cos(t) ⇒ Hypotenuse ÷ Base.
</p
